validity.recommendation: No action — the underlying cross-border proposal is real and still alive; keep Status = proposed.
validity.researcher_notes: Existence of the CONCEPT is well corroborated: a trilateral India-Myanmar-Bangladesh gas link has been discussed since 1997/2004-05 (trilateral talks, technical committee, abandoned when India declined Bangladesh transit-to-Nepal/Bhutan requests), revived in 2015 (Modi-Hasina), 2016 (Hydrocarbon Vision 2030), July 2023 and April 2024 (livemint, already the sheet's own [ref]), and — critically — is STILL active as of this month: Bangladesh's Power/Energy Minister proposed reopening pipeline talks with Myanmar's ambassador on 2026-08-02, reported independently by Prothom Alo (2026-08-04) and The Daily Star (Bangladesh's two largest English dailies, editorially independent of each other). So 'proposed' is the right status and is NOT stale under the dormancy rule (see status_reviews). No hallucination here.

validity.recommendation: Re-scope the row: either drop LengthKnown to blank/unknown and describe P0928 purely as the unbuilt cross-border concept (no fixed route/length has ever been agreed across any of its revivals), or split out the domestic NE-India grid buildout as a separate tracked item distinct from the cross-border spur. Do not keep citing the 2016 Hydrocarbon Vision 2030 total as 'this pipeline's' length.
validity.researcher_notes: P0928 conflates at least three distinct proposals of different vintage and scope under one entity: (1) the 1997/2005-06 bilateral/trilateral ~900 km Myanmar(Shwe field)-Bangladesh-India line, which never proceeded (Myanmar built the gas-to-China pipeline instead, operational since 2013 per kathmandupost.com); (2) India's 2016 'Hydrocarbon Vision 2030' domestic buildout for the north-east, which per The Economic Times (as reported independently by both Enerdata, 2016-08-17, and The Daily Star, 2016-08-16) comprises 'THIRTEEN ROUTES with a total length of about 6,900 km' of pipeline connecting NE Indian states/West Bengal to Chittagong (Bangladesh) and Sittwe (Myanmar) -- an aggregate multi-pipeline program, not a single line; and (3) the periodically-revived 2023-2026 cross-border talks (pipeline-journal 2023, livemint 2023/2024, Prothom Alo/Daily Star 2026) about a single bilateral/trilateral import line, which has never had a route, length, or gas-field source agreed (explicitly stated as still unresolved by Prothom Alo, 2026-08). GEM's wiki page (read for leads only, never cited) borrows the 6,900 km TOTAL FOR ALL THIRTEEN ROUTES and presents it as this one row's LengthKnown, which materially misstates what that number is.

validity.recommendation: Remove/blank LengthKnown=6900 for P0928 (or footnote heavily) — it is sourced only insofar as it is the printed total for a 13-route regional program, not a corroborated length for a single India-Myanmar-Bangladesh line.
validity.researcher_notes: Same two sources as the classification finding state explicitly: 'Thirteen routes with a total length of about 6,900 km of pipelines have been proposed for the purpose' (Daily Star, citing The Economic Times) — i.e. 6,900 km is a sum across 13 separate proposed pipelines for NE India's gas/LPG/diesel connectivity plan, most of which are domestic (e.g. the Contai-Haldia-Duttapulia line named in the same article), not one India-Myanmar-Bangladesh route. No source anywhere gives a length for a single cross-border line; Prothom Alo (2026-08-04) explicitly says of the currently-discussed pipeline that 'it remains unclear ... what route the pipeline would take' — i.e. there is still no length to cite for a real single pipeline as of today. Material disagreement between the sheet's implied claim (one pipeline, 6,900 km) and what the sources actually support (a 13-route program totaling 6,900 km) -> spec concern, not silently passed.

summary: P0928 (India-Myanmar-Bangladesh Gas Pipeline): existence/status confirmed (still genuinely proposed, freshly re-confirmed by Aug-2026 Bangladesh-Myanmar talks reported by Prothom Alo + Daily Star + Pipeline Technology Journal), but classification/spec concern -- LengthKnown=6,900 km is the printed total for a 13-route NE-India regional program (Hydrocarbon Vision 2030), not this single cross-border line's length -- plus an attribution concern on the Owner% split and a malformed Location cluster; FuelSource/Length/Owner/Location fills left UNRESOLVED rather than sourcing values tied to the wrong-scope project.
